content:
{'Turn 0': 'Tung Wah Group of Hospitals\' Universe Funeral Hall, located in Hung Hom, experienced a power system failure the day before yesterday (the 9th), affecting lighting, air conditioning, and exhaust systems in some of the funeral halls on various floors. Two days after the incident, the hall issued a notice today (the 11th) stating that some equipment was not operating as normal, and the funeral hall could only provide limited funeral hall rental services. A reporter visited the venue in the evening and found that some floors had individual funeral halls open. Relatives attending funerals said there was still no air conditioning in the halls, describing it as "very hot, but barely tolerable." Cheng Chi-kit, Chairman of the Funeral Services Association, visited the scene and said the funeral hall had identified the root cause of the problem, with improvements seen in a short time, and operations were "nearly back to normal." Tung Wah Group of Hospitals stated that after the failure, they had notified the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD) and contacted an engineering company for emergency repairs and partial power restoration, emphasizing that the mortuary storing bodies in the basement was not affected. Inspection revealed that the issue involved the busbar riser and fuse in the second-floor meter room, and it is not yet known whether this was related to high temperatures. All facilities are expected to be repaired by Thursday afternoon, at which point operations will return to normal. The FEHD stated that no requests for assistance from family members had been received, and would require the operator to submit a preliminary report and improvement measures within 7 working days from the date of the incident to prevent recurrence.'}

{'Turn 1': 'A citizen earlier posted on social media with a photo indicating that the Universe Funeral Hall had experienced a power outage the day before. (Threads photo)'}

{'Turn 2': 'A citizen posted on social media yesterday (the 10th) saying that the Universe Funeral Hall had experienced power system problems across the entire hall the day before, with the exhaust system malfunctioning, describing the scene as "filled with smoke," and noting that paper burning had to be suspended at the venue. An affected industry practitioner also posted that the funeral they were responsible for was originally scheduled to be held at this hall, but after negotiation, the funeral was transferred to another funeral hall, minimizing the impact.'}

{'Turn 3': 'Two days after the power outage, the Universe Funeral Hall issued a notice today stating that a power system failure had occurred the day before. After assessment by qualified engineering personnel, specific parts needed to be ordered for replacement, and it was estimated that repairs could not be completed in a short time. The notice also stated that some equipment in the hall was not operating normally, and the funeral hall could only provide limited funeral hall rental services with immediate effect. The notice also mentioned that for orders of funeral halls already rented, staff would contact the relevant funeral parlour operators in order of funeral dates to coordinate and follow up, and apologized for the inconvenience caused to those affected, describing it as a regrettable arrangement.'}

{'Turn 4': 'Two days after the power outage incident, the hall issued a notice this morning (the 11th) stating that some equipment was not operating normally and could only provide limited funeral hall rental services. (Website screenshot)'}

{'Turn 5': 'Some funeral halls without air conditioning; relatives say "very hot"; some power supply and exhaust functioning normally'}

{'Turn 6': 'According to website information, the Universe Funeral Hall has 5 ceremonial halls and 16 mourning rooms, each accommodating 40 to 180 people. A reporter visited the Universe Funeral Hall this evening and found that a relative leaving the venue said the funeral was held in a funeral hall on the 3rd floor, and felt there was no air conditioning in the hall, "very hot, but barely tolerable." A relative attending a funeral on the 4th floor said the air conditioning, elevators, and ventilation systems were all operating normally.'}

{'Turn 7': 'A florist working at the venue said that the funeral hall had opened two halls each on the 1st, 3rd, 4th, and 5th floors, with air conditioning and ventilation weaker in some halls, "very hot and smoky," but improved compared to the previous two days. The florist noted that two days ago during the power outage it was "filled with smoke," but families had "no choice" but to complete the ceremonies, and some families had to switch to Diamond Hill Funeral Hall or International Funeral Hall for their funerals.'}

{'Turn 8': 'Combining accounts from relatives attending funerals and florist staff, air conditioning in halls on some floors had returned to normal, but some halls remained "very hot and smoky."'}

{'Turn 9': 'Chairperson of Funeral Services Association: Operations nearly back to normal'}

{'Turn 10': 'Cheng Chi-kit, Chairman of the Funeral Services Association, visited the Universe Funeral Hall this afternoon to understand the situation, saying that "the overall situation is not seriously severe at this stage," and the funeral hall had identified the root cause of the power system problem, with improvements seen in a short time, "now nearly back to normal operations." There were no reports of chaos from families at the scene. He said that among the currently open halls, "the air conditioning intensity varies from hall to hall, some don\'t notice any problems, while others have some room for improvement," and considered that "the overall funeral has not been affected."'}

{'Turn 11': 'He emphasized that the power supply is still in the process of recovery and needs time, with some halls showing significant improvement and operating as normal. As for the less satisfactory halls, the funeral hall has made arrangements to transfer families to more suitable funeral halls, and if families do not wish to transfer, arrangements will still be made as usual, with at least the lighting system provided. He acknowledged that in the past only individual funeral halls had experienced malfunctions, "never had the entire building affected," but emphasized that based on current understanding, families or the public need not worry or panic.'}

{'Turn 12': 'The outside world is concerned about whether the bodies of the deceased have been affected by the power outage. Cheng Chi-kit said no related reports had been received so far, and emphasized that "if there were (any impact), families would definitely not compromise, everyone would know."'}

{'Turn 13': 'Cheng Chi-kit, Chairman of the Funeral Services Association, visited the scene today. He said the funeral hall was nearly back to normal operations and there was no need for excessive worry or panic. (News clip screenshot)'}

{'Turn 14': 'Tung Wah Group of Hospitals: Facilities expected to be repaired by Thursday afternoon'}

{'Turn 15': 'Tung Wah Group of Hospitals responded to inquiries stating that the power system failed the day before yesterday (the 9th). Inspection found that the issue involved the busbar riser and fuse in the second-floor meter room, with the specific cause under investigation, and it is not yet known whether this was related to high temperatures. The failure affected lighting, air conditioning, exhaust systems, and freight elevators in funeral halls on some floors, but the mortuary storing bodies in the basement was not affected. All facilities are expected to be repaired by Thursday afternoon, at which point operations will return to normal.'}

{'Turn 16': 'Tung Wah Group of Hospitals also stated that after the power failure at the hall, they had notified the FEHD and contacted an engineering company for emergency repairs and partial power restoration. The lighting, exhaust systems, and some air conditioning units in the affected funeral halls had resumed operation. Other air conditioning units and freight elevators were expected to take another two days to return to normal. The hospital authority expressed deep apologies to affected families and stated that rent refunds would be arranged for funeral parlour operators who had rented funeral halls, and funerals transferred to International Funeral Hall or Diamond Hill Funeral Hall would be provided free of charge without additional fees.'}

{'Turn 17': "The hospital authority also stated that the Universe Funeral Hall conducts regular power system inspections as required by law, and if the inspection reports contain any recommendations for replacement or improvement, they would be implemented as soon as possible to maintain normal operation of the hall's facilities, although the inspection reports showed everything was normal."}

{'Turn 18': 'The predecessor of the Universe Funeral Hall was the Hung Hom Public Funeral Hall of the Urban Council, which has been in operation for over 48 years. Tung Wah Group of Hospitals has won the operating rights twice for five-year terms since the end of 2018.'}

{'Turn 19': 'Predecessor was the Urban Council Hung Hom Public Funeral Hall; in operation for 48 years'}

{'Turn 20': 'According to records, the predecessor of the Universe Funeral Hall was the Hung Hom Public Funeral Hall of the Urban Council, which commenced operation in 1978. In early 2000, the FEHD outsourced funeral hall services through open tender. Tung Wah Group of Hospitals won the five-year operating rights at the end of 2018 and renamed it "Universe Funeral Hall," and won another five-year operating rights in 2024.'}

{'Turn 21': 'Dimsum Daily inquired with the FEHD about when the notification was received, whether the incident was related to aging hardware of the building, and what follow-up actions the FEHD was taking. The department replied in the evening that it was notified by the operator of the power failure on the afternoon of the 9th, and the specific cause of the failure was pending follow-up and investigation by the operator. The department also stated that the operator immediately took remedial measures at the time, including installing temporary devices in affected funeral halls to provide basic lighting and ventilation, or arranging transfers to the adjacent International Funeral Hall or rescheduling mourning dates with family consent. No requests for assistance from families had been received. The FEHD stated that it would urge the operator to resume full operations as soon as possible, requiring submission of a preliminary report and improvement measures within 7 working days from the date of the incident to prevent recurrence. The department would also review the report to assess whether additional measures are needed.'}
